# Installed-geometry EM sweep plan (P7d-4)

**Planning only — no solver was run and no coupling value exists here.** Generated by
`examples/em_sweep_plan.m` (`mission.EmSweepPlan`) from `rf_systems.csv`, `em_sweep_policy.csv` and
the antenna installation points of the simplified spacecraft. The CSVs are *derived* data: rerun the
script after changing those inputs. The plan tells the CST work what to solve and which solves fit
the Learning Edition; its results are imported as `coupling.CstS21Table` and used through
`coupling.CstCouplingModel`.

## Grids (`sweep_grids.csv`)

- **Coarse:** 1–27 GHz every 100 MHz (261 points) — the coarse S21(f) export grid.
- **Dense:** 41 points across each actual band, both edges included: S TM TX (2.2487–2.2513 GHz),
  S TC RX (2.0499–2.0501), GPS L1 RX (1.5652–1.5857), Ka TX (25.50–27.00), ISL TX/RX
  (10.465–10.485), and SAR TX/RX (9.3875–9.9125, **deferred**: closed network).

## Partition (`local_models.csv`, `pair_models.csv`, `band_feasibility.csv`)

The whole vehicle (6.38 × 2.38 × 2.33 m) cannot be meshed by the CST Learning Edition at any
frequency in the sweep, so the vehicle is split into:

- **LOCAL** — one 0.70 m box per antenna mount (8 models): installed pattern / near-structure
  effect (0.35 m from the 30–40 cm validity radius of the KARI RC-02 method);
- **PAIRWISE** — the box spanned by two antennas plus a 0.15 m margin (28 models), with the direct
  LOS status and blocking panels from the geometry evidence.

Feasibility uses a **lower-bound** hex-cell estimate
`cells ≥ ∏((extent + 2·0.25λ) / (λ/8))` against 100 000 cells (worker rules: 8 cells per
wavelength, Learning Edition limit). *Over the limit* is therefore certain; *within the limit* is
only possible (fine features such as probe gaps add cells; the accepted ISL model needed about
15× the bound).

## What the plan shows (2026-10-04)

- Whole vehicle: lower bound 7.8 × 10⁵ cells already at 1 GHz (1.3 × 10¹⁰ at 27 GHz).
- **Local boxes (0.7 m): full-wave feasible only up to ≈ 2.2 GHz.** So only the L-band (GPS) and
  S-band sweeps can be done locally at all; X-band ISL, Ka and SAR cannot be solved full-wave in
  the Learning Edition even for one antenna plus 35 cm of hull.
- **Pairs:** feasible up to 0.0–3.1 GHz (median 1.1 GHz); 12 of 28 pairs have no feasible
  frequency ≥ 1 GHz. Only the GPSA_1–GPSA_2 pair (1.1 m, clear LOS) reaches 3.1 GHz.
- **Pair × dense-band:** 32 of 216 (non-deferred) combinations are within the limit.

Consequence: installed-geometry coupling for the X-band and Ka bands needs a method other than
Learning-Edition full-wave (an asymptotic/PO/ray solver or a licensed solver); the S-band and
L-band pair coupling is feasible only for a handful of close pairs. Until such S21 tables exist,
`CstCouplingModel` reports `S21_UNAVAILABLE` and the analysis stays relative/pattern-based for those
pairs.
